newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian leaders denounce street protesters.
newsitem.headline: Albanian leaders denounce street protesters.

text.p: Albania's leadership on Wednesday denounced as undemocratic a wave of anti-government protests that have swept the impoverished Balkan nation and vowed to fight back with its own forces.

Prime Minister Aleksander Meksi's comments amounted to a barely veiled threat to crack down on demonstrations against the government's handling of the collapse of pyramid investment schemes, which have plunged Albania into crisis.
The prime minister suffered a setback on Tuesday when members of his ruling Democratic Party objected to his proposal to declare emergency rule to quell unrest in the port of Vlore.

The Democratic Forum, a cross-party opposition alliance, called for a midday rally in Tirana's main Skanderbeg Square on Wednesday. Eyewitnesses said the square was teeming with police, many in plain clothes. There was no sign of any rally being organised.
"The Democratic Party has organised to respond with our forces, not only the police," Meksi told Reuters television. "We are ready."

On Wednesday, some 150 demonstrators briefly gathered on the square and shouted "Vlore! Vlore!", then scattered to dodge truckloads of riot police. Security forces broke up an opposition rally in Tirana last weekend.
In Vlore, some 5,000 protesters gathered for what has now become a daily ritual, shouting "No to dictatorship" and denouncing President Sali Berisha.
The impoverished port was the scene of two days of street battles between protesters and riot police which left three dead and scores injured.
The town's newly-installed police chief said it was his first priority to open a dialogue with the protesters, nearly all of whom have sunk money into a local investment fund which folded last week.
"We will protect the peaceful protesters," police chief Ethem Kurti told Reuters.
At least 30,000 mourners streamed through the town's streets on Tuesday in an outpouring of emotion at the funeral of a 33-year-old shop owner killed in the clashes on Monday.
Marchers shouted "The police killed him!" and blamed Berisha for the loss of what little money they had accumulated in Europe's poorest country.

Meksi proposed emergency rule in Vlore, including deployment of the army, after blaming leftist extremists for the unrest. Local Democratic Party deputies urged their leaders to think again and step back from the brink of civil war.
Democratic Party leaders were expected to meet later in the day to consider their next steps.
Opposition parties blame Berisha's right-wing government, which has ruled Albania since 1992, of dipping into funds from the scheme to finance the Democratic Party's re-election campaign last year.

The Forum for Democracy alliance stayed away from talks with authorities last week to discuss the pyramid scandal on grounds that it was a "publicity stunt". But it says it favours dialogue in order to form a "technocrat government".
Meksi accused the opposition of using the crisis to destablise the country. "Our party has proposed talks with the other parties but...they have chosen violence, not dialogue. They want a civil war."
